_about: Hook patterns for the copy step (factory/lib/copy.cjs). Evidence and sources: docs/viral-playbook-2026-11-12.md. The examples show the STRUCTURE only; the brain writes the real hook for each job (AGENTS.md rule 3). Every hook: 6 words or fewer, no digits, no brand name, no guarantee, and the first frame must show what the line says.

patterns.how: Open on the finished result; the line names what the viewer already sees working.
patterns.first_frame: The result itself at 0.0 s: the organised screen, the booking message arriving, the calm owner.
patterns.evidence: OpusClip 34,635 clips: best hook type; ViralVideoSearch: 53% of viral videos open on a visual hook.
patterns.honesty: Show only what the product really does. No invented results or numbers.

patterns.how: Name the daily pain in the viewer's own words, in the first three words.
patterns.first_frame: The pain happening: messages flooding in, a phone ringing unanswered, a stressed face.
patterns.evidence: Chinese pain-point hook family; best average watch time on @sudegy.clients before 2026-11-12 (smart-funnel).
patterns.honesty: A pain the vertical really has (sudegy_brain VERTICALS). No statistics.

patterns.how: Reject a common belief in one short line; the video then backs it up.
patterns.first_frame: The believed thing with a red mark landing on it, or a character shaking the head at it.
patterns.evidence: ContentLabs 3,997 videos: hot-take openings averaged about 140K views; OpusClip contrarian type.
patterns.honesty: Only when the body of the video supports the claim. Never attack a named competitor.

patterns.how: A short command plus what is at stake; the viewer learns what to check before losing something real.
patterns.first_frame: A character raising a hand to stop, or an alarm light, next to the risky thing.
patterns.evidence: ContentLabs: fear (something to lose) led on average views; OpusClip imperative type; Douyin formula «千万不要…».
patterns.honesty: The risk must be real and stated plainly. No scare tactics, no medical or financial threats.

patterns.how: Open an everyday mystery the viewer has noticed but never solved; answer it in the video.
patterns.first_frame: The puzzle in the picture: a customer bubble that vanishes, question marks over the owner.
patterns.evidence: ContentLabs: investigator openings about 140K average views; ViralVideoSearch: curiosity gap opens 14% of viral videos.
patterns.honesty: The video must answer the question it opens.

patterns.how: Call the exact viewer by role, then the stake.
patterns.first_frame: A character pointing at the camera with the role written on a tag.
patterns.evidence: Chinese belonging and identity hook family (人人都是产品经理, 120 Douyin openings).
patterns.honesty: Use only when the video is truly for that role.

patterns.how: Promise a small counted list the video then shows, one item per scene.
patterns.first_frame: The count as a big card and the first item already appearing.
patterns.honesty: The number counts items shown in THIS video, written as a word. Never a result, a price or a statistic.

patterns.how: Drop the viewer inside a familiar moment; no explanation first.
patterns.first_frame: The moment already in progress with an exaggerated reaction.
patterns.evidence: Revid 176,367 TikToks: POV had the highest median views of any shooting style (107K).
patterns.honesty: An everyday moment, not a fake customer story.

patterns.how: Offer something worth saving: a checklist, a self-test, a template shown fully on screen.
patterns.first_frame: The checklist card on screen from the first frame, first line readable.
patterns.evidence: ContentLabs: proof-drop hooks earned the most saves (1,761 average); Douyin ranks save and save-plus-return.
patterns.honesty: The whole list is shown in the video. Never promise to send anything.

patterns.how: A real credential, then the thing nobody tells you.
patterns.first_frame: The expert character with a badge, already mid-gesture.
patterns.evidence: OpusClip: expert-explainer was the most common storyline (2,626 clips).
patterns.honesty: Only credentials listed in the client's facts. Never invent years, titles or client counts.

weak_openers._about: Openings that underperformed in the OpusClip and ContentLabs datasets. The copy gate rejects a hook that starts with any of these.

emotions._about: ContentLabs 3,997 videos (averages, one vendor, directional). Pick ONE per video.
emotions.fear: something real to lose; led on views
emotions.empathy: a moment the viewer lives every day; led on shares
emotions.outrage: a common unfairness; led on comments. Keep it fair and never aimed at a named party
emotions.curiosity: a gap to close; solid middle
emotions.trust: useful and checkable; led on saves
emotions.avoid: aspiration and hope were the weakest
